answer: An agent economy can use staked, endorsed identities: every agent locks collateral at a unique vertex of a trust graph and earns voting weight only through vouchers from already-staked peers. A hollow account with no backers carries zero weight, and a mirror of another agent fails because vault keys and voucher history differ. To mount a Sybil attack, an adversary must fund a fresh stake and buy endorsements for each fake identity, so the cost scales linearly with each new vertex while honest agents gain compounding trust.
